name: Shop_SellFromPartyMember

score.note: Improved from 231/110 to 168/42 (byte size still matches exactly, 540/540) by fixing two concrete, evidence-backed bugs found by decompiling the actual reference machine code with m2c (see tools/compiler families transplant's m2c/target.lst, which prints the reference disassembly with real addresses/labels): (1) Shop_DrawItemPrice's first argument was wrongly `price_window` (the per-redraw window created inside redraw_page, offset sp+0x10) when the reference clearly passes `list_window` (the window created once before redraw_page, offset sp+0xC) -- Func_080b110c(spC, ...) in the m2c output. This single fix alone dropped the diff from 231 to 172 because it had been inflating price_window's apparent use-density enough to win the function's single remaining callee-saved register (fp) over `shop`, cascading into wrong register/stack assignments through the whole function body. (2) Declaring `unit` before `list_window` (their true relative order, matching m2c) rather than after fixed a residual sp+8/sp+12 slot swap between them (172 -> 168), and writing selection's -1/+1 cursor-move updates as a separate `selection -= 1;`/`selection += 1;` statement before the Modulo() call (matching the reference's standalone `subs r7,#1` before the add, instead of folding the -1 into one expression) fixed a small instruction-order mismatch (wrong_instructions 46 -> 42, though total differing_halfwords stayed 168 because of an unrelated compensating shift -- see below). After these fixes every remaining diff line (verified by grepping the --align output) traces to exactly one thing: the reference splits its literal-constant pool into two clusters -- an early one right after shop->mode=3 holding {Data_03001f2c_a (SHOP_RUNTIME address), 0x1ff (item-id mask)} with a `b.n`-over-data skip, and a late one near the function's end holding the remaining 4 words -- while our compiled candidate (verified via `xgcc -S` on this exact source with the exact approved flags) emits ONE combined 6-word table (.L30) at the end, matching neither ARM range pressure (540 bytes is comfortably inside Thumb's 1020-byte pc-relative reach either way) nor anything we could tie to a specific C-level idiom. Every '!' and '+/-' line in the final --align diff is a pc-relative offset or branch-target shift downstream of this one 8-byte pool-placement difference (confirmed: the only true content difference left is the trailing block of instructions, which is exactly the reference's missing/candidate's extra 2 pool words disassembled as garbage `movs r0,r0`/`lsls`/`subs` opcodes).

rejected_experiments: for(;;){ if(redraw){...} } inner loop with window/x/y as plain expressions (no temps): 536 candidate bytes vs 540 reference, worse than the temp-var version.

do { ... } while (1) restatement of the inner loop: byte-identical output to the for(;;) version, no change (536/544-byte families depending on companion edits) -- confirms the layout choice is not driven by loop-statement syntax.

Plain for(;;) nested loop with `break`/`continue` (no goto): compiled to 544 candidate bytes vs 540 reference; the goto-based rewrite matching the disassembly's exact label graph fixed the size mismatch to 540/540 but did not close the remaining register-role differences.

2026-08-27 session, after the two real fixes above (score frozen at 168/42), tried to close the remaining literal-pool-split gap: combined-decl-and-init for `shop` (`struct ShopRuntime *shop = SHOP_RUNTIME;`), reordering local declarations several ways (price_window first, shop first, unit/list_window swapped -- this last one was the real fix above, everything else was a no-op), inlining the Shop_PlaceCursor y-argument vs a named `y` temp (byte-for-byte identical output either way), reassociating `selection - 1 + item_count` into `item_count + selection - 1` etc. via the permuter's PERM_GENERAL over 4 alternatives per branch (all 16 combinations scored identically, 168 -- GCC's tree canonicalizes commutative + regardless of source spelling), and swapping the 0x1ff mask's operand order in `item_id = 0x1ff & unit->inventory[selection]`. None changed the score by even one bit. Confirmed via `xgcc -S` (approved flags, no invented options) that GCC's own RTL/assembly-emission stage already produces a single combined literal table `.L30` for our source -- the reference's two-cluster layout is a machine_dependent_reorg (arm.c minipool) decision that appears in the final assembled bytes but is not visibly driven by anything in the .s output, and no combination of purely-cosmetic source rewrites tried moved it. This residual likely needs either a genuinely different (not yet identified) control-flow/statement shape somewhere in the function, or is simply not reachable through ordinary C source variation and should be treated as the honest last-mile floor for this owner absent a new idea.
notes: Recovered only from the retained owner assembly, approved local ROM, the byte-exact template/sibling sources, in-repository headers, and the approved compiler.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.

Twin of 0x080b211c (shop/select_party_member.c family): diffing games/gs1/asm/080b1bd0.s against games/gs1/asm/080b211c.s shows the two are near line-identical raw disassembly, differing only in which price/name callee they invoke (Func_080b19cc Shop_ComputeSalePrice vs Func_080b20e8 Shop_ComputeRepairPrice), literal-pool offsets, and one extra block at the end of 080b1bd0 (a call to Shop_SelectSaleQuantity + Func_080b1f4c that 080b211c's flow replaces with a single call to Func_080b2328) -- confirming 080b1bd0 is the 'sell an item from this party member' flow reached when shop->party_action == 1 in shop/select_party_member.c, and 080b211c is the parallel 'repair' flow.

2026-08-27: this owner's Shop_DrawItemPrice call had a real bug (fixed this session, see score note) where the once-created outer window (here, list_window) rather than the per-redraw window (price_window) was the correct first argument -- found by decompiling games/gs1/asm/080b1bd0.s's own reference bytes with m2c via `tools/compiler families transplant`. Given how closely 080b211c mirrors this file's raw disassembly, its analogous price/repair-drawing call very likely has the same once-created-vs-per-redraw window mix-up; whoever works 080b211c next should check its own m2c/target.lst before trusting its current argument order (not edited here, per the task's file-isolation rule).

Ability_GetAvailability(unit_id) is reused here as an item-availability *count* (its return value minus one clamps the selection index), not just the boolean sense used in draw_party_member_item_grid.c/select_party_member.c -- both usages are consistent with a single s32-returning function.

Value_00000075 and Value_00000caa are placeholder message-id symbols named after their own address value (the repo's existing Value_XXXXXXXX convention, e.g. select_sale_quantity.c's Value_00000cad); their real message text was not resolved.
